title: Sea Levels Around the World Are Much Higher Than We Thought

mock_data.title: Sea Levels Around the World Are Much Higher Than We Thought
mock_data.passage:
Almost all research on the impacts of future sea-level rise has assumed today's sea levels are lower than they actually are due to a "methodological blind spot". That means flooding and erosion will happen sooner than expected.

Katharina Seeger and Philip Minderhoud, both at Wageningen University in the Netherlands, analysed 385 peer-reviewed studies on coastal vulnerability and found that 90 per cent failed to consider the effects of ocean currents, tides, temperature, salinity and winds on sea level. As a result, they underestimated the water level at the coast by an average of 24 to 27 centimetres.

Once corrected, the number of people whose homes will be underwater by 2100 could increase by up to 68 per cent, or 132 million additional people. The bulk of them are in South-East Asia and Oceania, where sea levels are on average 1 metre higher than previously thought, and several metres in some areas.

"If a representative from a place like that comes to a global gathering and tries to gather support… it can be quite frustrating if there's this type of scientific assessment that actually says… it will only be affected in the next century, while in reality the area is actually much more exposed," said Minderhoud at a briefing.

Projections that sea levels will rise by up to 1 metre by the end of the century are still accurate. But since most research on the consequences of this rise started with a baseline that was too low, these impacts will happen sooner than forecast.

Forty-six of the studies were cited in the latest round of reports by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the most authoritative statement on warming effects, including sea-level rise.

Earth bulges at the equator due to its rotation, and denser parts of its mantle exert a greater gravitational pull on any water above them. So determining the elevation of a given point requires a computer model of the geoid, an irregular shape that represents mean sea level around the world.

But actual sea level can be several metres higher than the geoid in places where winds or currents pile up water, for example, or where warmer temperatures cause water to expand. And coastlines can move up or down as rivers build up sediment or cities suck groundwater out from underneath them.

Rather than figuring out the elevation of water and land at the coast by comparing satellite measurements with the geoid, the majority of researchers simply used the unadjusted geoid sea level. And even those who did the calculations mostly botched them, often because they determined land and sea elevations with different geoid models. Less than 1 per cent of the studies found the correct current sea level for the coastlines they were studying.

Climate scientists and oceanographers who study sea-level rise should work more closely with the geographers, environmental scientists and others who study coastal impacts, says Matt Palmer at the Met Office, the UK's national weather service.

"You could call it lost in translation," he says. "It's important that that last mile is done well, otherwise it kind of undermines the whole enterprise."

The problem is one of climate justice, says Palmer. Underestimates of sea level have been particularly egregious in parts of lower-income countries, such as river deltas in Africa and Asia, partly because data on variations in gravity is sparser there, making the geoid less accurate. But these are also the areas most vulnerable to sea level rise.

The scientific community should gather more data in lower-income countries, especially by installing tide gauges to measure sea level, says Joanne Williams at the UK National Oceanography Centre.

"There are many factors that affect sea level at the coast, some of which are quite localised, so the gold standard remains local, long-term, well-calibrated measurements," she says.

Katharina Seeger and Philip Minderhoud from Wageningen University in the Netherlands studied 385 reports. They found that 90% of these reports didn't think about things like ocean currents, tides, temperature, and wind. These things change the sea level. Because of this, the reports underestimated how high the water would be at the coast. They were wrong by about 24 to 27 centimetres.

Most of these people live in South-East Asia and Oceania. In these areas, sea levels are about 1 metre higher than we thought. In some places, they are even several metres higher.

Minderhoud said that people from these areas might have problems getting help. If reports say their area won't be affected for a long time, but it really is, it can be frustrating. They need help now, not later.

Forty-six of these reports were used in the newest reports from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The IPCC is the most important group that talks about the effects of climate change, including rising sea levels.

But the real sea level can be higher than the geoid in some places. This can happen where winds or currents push water together, or where warm temperatures make the water expand. Also, coastlines can move up or down as rivers bring sand and soil, or as cities take water out of the ground.

Most researchers didn't find the height of the water and land by comparing satellite pictures with the geoid. They just used the geoid sea level without changing it. And even the ones who did the calculations often made mistakes. They used different geoid models for the land and the sea. Less than 1% of the reports found the correct sea level for the coastlines they were studying.

Matt Palmer from the Met Office, the UK's weather service, says that climate scientists and oceanographers should work more with people who study coasts. This includes geographers and environmental scientists.

He said it's like something got lost in translation. It's important to do the last step correctly, or it makes everything else worthless.

mock_data.passageB2:
New research suggests that previous studies on the impact of rising sea levels have been based on inaccurate data. Almost all studies have underestimated current sea levels because they haven't fully considered certain factors. This oversight means that coastal flooding and erosion could happen sooner and be more severe than previously thought.

Katharina Seeger and Philip Minderhoud from Wageningen University in the Netherlands scrutinized 385 scientific studies about how vulnerable coastlines are. They found that 90% of these studies didn't properly consider the impact of ocean currents, tides, temperature, salt levels, and winds on sea levels. Because of this, they calculated that the actual water level at the coast was, on average, 24 to 27 centimetres higher than their estimates.

When these adjustments are made, the number of people whose homes could be underwater by 2100 could rise by as much as 68%, adding 132 million people to the total. Most of these people live in South-East Asia and Oceania, where sea levels are, on average, 1 metre higher than previously believed, and in some places, several metres higher.

Minderhoud explained at a briefing that if representatives from affected areas attend international meetings to ask for help, it can be frustrating if scientific assessments suggest that the impact won't be felt until later in the century, when the area is already at risk.

The projections that sea levels will rise by up to 1 metre by the end of the century are still considered accurate. However, because most research on the effects of this rise started with a flawed baseline, the consequences will be felt sooner than predicted.

Forty-six of these studies were used in the latest reports by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The IPCC reports are the most authoritative source of information on the effects of global warming, including rising sea levels.

The Earth bulges at the equator because of its rotation, and denser parts of the Earth's mantle have a stronger gravitational pull on the water above them. To determine the exact height of a location, scientists use a computer model of the geoid. The geoid is an irregular shape that represents the average sea level around the world.

However, the actual sea level can be several metres higher than the geoid in areas where winds or currents push water together, or where warmer temperatures cause the water to expand. Also, coastlines can rise or fall as rivers deposit sediment or as cities pump out groundwater from beneath them. These are examples of dynamic processes that impact local sea levels.

Instead of calculating the height of water and land at the coast by comparing satellite measurements to the geoid, most researchers simply used the geoid sea level without making any corrections. Even those who attempted to make corrections often did so incorrectly, usually because they used different geoid models to determine the height of land and sea. Less than 1% of the studies correctly calculated the current sea level for the coastlines they were studying. This is a significant problem.

Matt Palmer from the Met Office, the UK's national weather service, believes that climate scientists and oceanographers who study rising sea levels should work more closely with geographers, environmental scientists, and others who study the impact on coastlines. This collaboration is essential for accurate predictions.

Palmer describes the issue as a communication breakdown. He states that it's crucial to get the final details right, otherwise the entire effort is undermined. Proper communication and interdisciplinary work is key to mitigating the issue.

Palmer emphasizes that this is an issue of climate justice. The underestimation of sea levels has been particularly pronounced in poorer countries, such as river deltas in Africa and Asia. This is partly because there is less data available on gravity variations in these areas, which makes the geoid less accurate. However, these are also the areas that are most vulnerable to rising sea levels.

Joanne Williams from the UK National Oceanography Centre suggests that the scientific community should gather more data in poorer countries, especially by installing tide gauges to measure sea level. This would help to rectify the gaps in data and improve future predictions.

Williams explains that many factors affect sea level at the coast, some of which are quite localized. Therefore, the best approach is to have local, long-term, and well-calibrated measurements. This is considered the gold standard for accurate sea-level data.
mock_data.passageC1:
A critical oversight, a methodological blind spot, has been identified in the vast majority of research pertaining to the projected impacts of sea-level rise, indicating that current understandings may significantly underestimate the immediacy of coastal inundation and erosion. The prevailing assumption that present-day sea levels serve as an accurate baseline is, according to new research, fundamentally flawed.

In their analysis of 385 peer-reviewed studies on coastal vulnerability, Katharina Seeger and Philip Minderhoud of Wageningen University in the Netherlands, determined that a staggering 90% failed to account for the dynamic influence of ocean currents, tidal patterns, temperature variations, salinity gradients, and wind forces on sea level. This omission, they contend, has led to a systematic underestimation of coastal water levels, averaging between 24 and 27 centimetres.

The implications of this correction are profound. Once this previously unacknowledged factor is integrated into predictive models, the number of individuals facing potential displacement due to submerged coastal areas by the year 2100 could escalate by as much as 68%, translating to an additional 132 million people. The epicentre of this heightened vulnerability lies in South-East Asia and Oceania, regions where actual sea levels are, on average, a metre higher than previously estimated, with localized areas exhibiting discrepancies reaching several metres. This necessitates a recalibration of risk assessments and adaptation strategies.

Minderhoud articulated the potential ramifications at a recent briefing, highlighting the potential for disenfranchisement. "If representatives from highly vulnerable regions attend global forums seeking support, their efforts could be undermined by scientific assessments that, due to flawed baselines, project impacts occurring later than is realistically the case. The lived reality, he emphasized, is that these areas are already far more exposed than current models suggest.

While existing projections forecasting a sea-level rise of up to 1 metre by the end of the century remain technically accurate, the consequences are poised to manifest considerably sooner than originally anticipated. Given that the majority of impact assessments have been predicated on an artificially low baseline, the temporal window for effective mitigation and adaptation is demonstrably shrinking. This necessitates a proactive approach to coastal management.

Significantly, forty-six of the studies flagged for their methodological shortcomings were cited in the latest Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports, the foremost authoritative source on the multifaceted effects of global warming, including sea-level rise. This raises concerns about the robustness of current global policy frameworks and underscores the urgent need for a comprehensive re-evaluation of existing data.

The Earth's rotation engenders an equatorial bulge, while variations in mantle density exert a gravitational pull on overlying water masses. Consequently, determining the precise elevation of any given point necessitates the utilization of a geoid model, a complex computational representation of mean sea level across the globe. However, actual sea levels can deviate significantly from the geoid, influenced by factors such as wind-driven water accumulation and thermal expansion. Moreover, coastlines are dynamic entities, subject to vertical movement driven by sediment deposition and groundwater extraction.

Regrettably, the majority of researchers have relied on unadjusted geoid sea levels, rather than undertaking the meticulous task of reconciling satellite measurements with geoid models to ascertain accurate coastal elevations. Even among those who attempted such calculations, errors were commonplace, often stemming from inconsistencies in the geoid models employed for land and sea elevation measurements. Alarmingly, less than 1% of the studies reviewed accurately determined the current sea level for the coastlines under investigation, calling into question the reliability of a significant body of research.

Matt Palmer of the Met Office, the UK's national weather service, advocates for closer collaboration between climate scientists and oceanographers specializing in sea-level rise, and geographers and environmental scientists focusing on coastal impacts. He suggests that a breakdown in communication, a disconnect between disciplines, may be at the root of the problem.

Palmer posits that the issue is fundamentally one of climate justice. The underestimation of sea levels has been particularly acute in lower-income nations, notably in river deltas across Africa and Asia. This disparity is partly attributable to a scarcity of data on gravity variations in these regions, leading to less precise geoid models. Ironically, these are precisely the areas that are most susceptible to the adverse effects of sea-level rise, thereby exacerbating existing inequalities.

To rectify this imbalance, Joanne Williams of the UK National Oceanography Centre, emphasizes the imperative for the scientific community to augment data collection in lower-income countries, prioritizing the deployment of tide gauges for precise sea-level measurements. These local, long-term, well-calibrated measurements are considered the gold standard for understanding coastal sea-level dynamics, particularly given the multitude of localized factors that can influence sea levels, making them indispensable for accurate risk assessment and informed policy decisions. This is where real progress can take root.

mock_data.translation:
Kelajakdagi dengiz sathi ko'tarilishining ta'sirlari bo'yicha deyarli barcha tadqiqotlar bugungi dengiz sathini "metodologik ko'r nuqta" tufayli haqiqatda bo'lganidan pastroq deb taxmin qilgan. Bu suv toshqini va eroziya kutilganidan tezroq sodir bo'lishini anglatadi.

Niderlandiyadagi Vageningen universitetidagi Katarina Zeger va Filip Minderhoud qirg'oq zaifligiga oid 385 ta ekspert tekshiruvidan o'tgan tadqiqotni tahlil qildilar va 90 foizi okean oqimlari, suv ko'tarilishi va tushishi, harorat, sho'rlik va shamollarning dengiz sathiga ta'sirini hisobga olmagan. Natijada, ular qirg'oqdagi suv sathini o'rtacha 24 dan 27 santimetrgacha past baholadilar.

Tuzatilgandan so'ng, 2100 yilga kelib uylari suv ostida qoladigan odamlar soni 68 foizga yoki qo'shimcha 132 million kishiga oshishi mumkin. Ularning asosiy qismi Janubi-Sharqiy Osiyo va Okeaniyada joylashgan bo'lib, u yerda dengiz sathi oldin o'ylanganidan o'rtacha 1 metrga yuqori va ba'zi hududlarda bir necha metrga.

"Agar ana shunday joydan kelgan vakil global yig'ilishga kelib, qo'llab-quvvatlash to'plashga harakat qilsa... agar haqiqatan ham shunday ilmiy baho bo'lsa, bu juda asabiylashtiradigan bo'lishi mumkin... keyingi asrda ta'sirlanadi, aslida esa hudud ancha ko'proq xavf ostida," dedi Minderhoud brifingda.

Asr oxiriga kelib dengiz sathi 1 metrgacha ko'tarilishi haqidagi bashoratlar hali ham aniq. Ammo bu ko'tarilishning oqibatlari bo'yicha aksariyat tadqiqotlar juda past boshlang'ich nuqtadan boshlanganligi sababli, bu ta'sirlar prognoz qilinganidan tezroq sodir bo'ladi.

Tadqiqotlarning qirq oltitasi Iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha hukumatlararo guruhning dengiz sathi ko'tarilishi ham kirgan isish ta'sirlari bo'yicha eng ishonchli bayonot bo'lgan eng so'nggi hisobotlarida keltirilgan.

Yer ekvator atrofida aylanishi tufayli bo'rtadi va uning mantiyasining zichroq qismlari ustidagi har qanday suvga kattaroq gravitatsion tortishish kuchini ta'sir qiladi. Shunday qilib, berilgan nuqtaning balandligini aniqlash geoid kompyuter modelini talab qiladi, bu dunyo bo'ylab o'rtacha dengiz sathini ifodalovchi tartibsiz shakl.

Ammo haqiqiy dengiz sathi shamollar yoki oqimlar suvni to'playdigan joylarda yoki issiqroq harorat suvning kengayishiga sabab bo'ladigan joylarda geoiddan bir necha metr balandroq bo'lishi mumkin. Va qirg'oq chiziqlari daryolar cho'kindi to'plaganida yoki shaharlar er ostidagi suvni so'rib olganda ko'tarilishi yoki tushishi mumkin.

Qirg'oqdagi suv va quruqlik balandligini sun'iy yo'ldosh o'lchovlarini geoid bilan solishtirish orqali aniqlash o'rniga, tadqiqotchilarning aksariyati oddiygina tuzatilmagan geoid dengiz sathidan foydalangan. Va hatto hisob-kitoblarni amalga oshirganlar ham ko'pincha ularni noto'g'ri bajargan, ko'pincha quruqlik va dengiz balandliklarini turli geoid modellari bilan aniqlanganligi sababli. Tadqiqotlarning 1 foizdan kamrog'i o'rganayotgan qirg'oq chiziqlari uchun to'g'ri joriy dengiz sathini aniqlagan.

Dengiz sathi ko'tarilishini o'rganadigan iqlim olimlari va okeanograflar qirg'oq ta'sirlarini o'rganadigan geograflar, atrof-muhit olimlari va boshqalar bilan yaqinroq ishlashlari kerak, deydi Buyuk Britaniyaning milliy ob-havo xizmatidagi Met Officedagi Mett Palmer.

"Buni tarjimada yo'qolgan deb atash mumkin," deydi u. "Oxirgi milning yaxshi bajarilishi muhim, aks holda bu butun tashabbusni zaiflashtiradi."

Muammo iqlim adolati masalasi, deydi Palmer. Dengiz sathini past baholash past daromadli mamlakatlarning ba'zi qismlarida, masalan Afrika va Osiyodagi daryo deltalarida, ayniqsa dahshatli bo'lgan, qisman gravitatsiyadagi o'zgarishlar haqidagi ma'lumotlar u yerda kamroq bo'lganligi sababli geoidni kamroq aniq qiladi. Ammo bular dengiz sathi ko'tarilishiga eng zaif hududlar ham.

Ilmiy jamoa past daromadli mamlakatlarda ko'proq ma'lumot to'plashi kerak, ayniqsa dengiz sathini o'lchash uchun suv ko'tarilish o'lchagichlarini o'rnatish orqali, deydi Buyuk Britaniya Milliy Okeanografiya Markazidagi Joann Uilyams.

"Qirg'oqda dengiz sathiga ta'sir qiladigan ko'plab omillar bor, ularning ba'zilari ancha mahalliy, shuning uchun oltin standart mahalliy, uzoq muddatli, yaxshi kalibrlangan o'lchovlar bo'lib qoladi," deydi u.

mock_data.translationB1:
Dengiz sathining ko'tarilishi haqidagi tadqiqotlar aniq bo'lmasligi mumkin. Ular dengiz sathiga ta'sir qiluvchi barcha omillarni ko'rib chiqmaganligi sababli xato bo'lishi mumkin. Bu shuni anglatadiki, toshqinlar va eroziya biz o'ylaganimizdan ham tezroq sodir bo'lishi mumkin.

Niderlandiyaning Wageningen universitetidan Katharina Seeger va Philip Minderhoud 385 ta hisobotni o'rganib chiqdi. Ular ushbu hisobotlarning 90 foizi okean oqimlari, suv toshqinlari, harorat va shamol kabi narsalar haqida o'ylamaganligini aniqladilar. Bu narsalar dengiz sathini o'zgartiradi. Shu sababli, hisobotlar qirg'oqda suv qanchalik baland bo'lishini kam baholagan. Ular taxminan 24 dan 27 santimetrgacha xato qilishgan.

Agar biz bu xatoni tuzatsak, 2100 yilga kelib yanada ko'proq odamlarning uylari suv ostida qolishi mumkin. 68% gacha ko'proq odam, yoki 132 million kishi ta'sirlanishi mumkin. Bu odamlarning aksariyati Janubi-Sharqiy Osiyo va Okeaniyada yashaydi. Bu hududlarda dengiz sathi biz o'ylaganimizdan taxminan 1 metr yuqoriroq. Ba'zi joylarda esa bir necha metr yuqori.

Minderhoudning aytishicha, bu hududlardan bo'lgan odamlarga yordam olishda muammolar bo'lishi mumkin. Agar hisobotlar ularning hududiga uzoq vaqt davomida ta'sir qilmaydi desa, lekin aslida shunday bo'lsa, bu tushkunlikka olib kelishi mumkin. Ularga keyin emas, hozir yordam kerak.

Olimlar hali ham dengiz sathi asr oxirigacha 1 metrgacha ko'tariladi deb o'ylashadi. Ammo hisobotlar noto'g'ri dengiz sathidan boshlanganligi sababli, bu ko'tarilishning ta'siri biz o'ylaganimizdan ham tezroq sodir bo'ladi.

Ushbu hisobotlarning qirq oltitasi Iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha hukumatlararo panelning (IPCC) eng yangi hisobotlarida ishlatilgan. IPCC - bu iqlim o'zgarishining, shu jumladan dengiz sathining ko'tarilishining oqibatlari haqida gapiradigan eng muhim guruh.

Yer o'z o'qi atrofida aylangani uchun ekvatorda kengroq. Bundan tashqari, Yerning ba'zi qismlari suvni kuchliroq tortadi. Joy qanchalik baland ekanligini aniqlash uchun bizga maxsus kompyuter modeli kerak. Bu model dunyo bo'ylab o'rtacha dengiz sathini ko'rsatadi. U geoid deb ataladi.

Ammo haqiqiy dengiz sathi ba'zi joylarda geoiddan yuqori bo'lishi mumkin. Bu shamol yoki oqimlar suvni birga itarib yuborgan yoki iliq harorat suvning kengayishiga olib kelgan joylarda sodir bo'lishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, daryolar qum va tuproq olib kelishi yoki shaharlar yerdan suv chiqarib olishi bilan qirg'oq chiziqlari yuqoriga yoki pastga harakatlanishi mumkin.

Ko'pgina tadqiqotchilar suv va quruqlikning balandligini sun'iy yo'ldosh rasmlarini geoid bilan solishtirish orqali topmadilar. Ular shunchaki geoid dengiz sathidan o'zgartirmasdan foydalanishdi. Va hatto hisob-kitoblarni qilganlar ham ko'pincha xatolarga yo'l qo'yishdi. Ular quruqlik va dengiz uchun turli geoid modellaridan foydalanishdi. Hisobotlarning 1 foizdan kamrog'i o'rganilayotgan qirg'oq chiziqlari uchun to'g'ri dengiz sathini topdi.

Buyuk Britaniyaning ob-havo xizmati bo'lgan Met Officedan Matt Palmerning aytishicha, iqlimshunoslar va okeanograflar qirg'oqlarni o'rganuvchi odamlar bilan ko'proq ishlashlari kerak. Bularga geograflar va ekologlar kiradi.

Uning so'zlariga ko'ra, bu tarjimada nimadir yo'qolganiga o'xshaydi. Oxirgi qadamni to'g'ri bajarish muhim, aks holda hamma narsa befoyda bo'lib qoladi.

Palmerning aytishicha, bu iqlim adolati muammosi. Dengiz sathi haqidagi xatolar kambag'al mamlakatlarda yomonroq. Buning sababi, bu hududlarda tortishish kuchi haqida unchalik ko'p ma'lumot yo'q, shuning uchun geoid unchalik aniq emas. Ammo bu shuningdek, dengiz sathining ko'tarilishiga eng zaif bo'lgan hududlar hamdir.

Buyuk Britaniya Milliy Okeanografiya markazidan Joanne Williamsning aytishicha, olimlar kambag'al mamlakatlarda ko'proq ma'lumot to'plashlari kerak. Ular dengiz sathini o'lchash uchun to'lqin o'lchagichlarini o'rnatishlari kerak.

Uning aytishicha, qirg'oqda dengiz sathiga ko'p narsa ta'sir qiladi. Bu narsalarning ba'zilari faqat kichik hududlarga ta'sir qiladi. Shunday qilib, eng yaxshi narsa - ehtiyotkorlik bilan amalga oshirilgan mahalliy, uzoq muddatli o'lchovlarga ega bo'lish.

Joyning aniq balandligini aniqlash uchun olimlar geoidning kompyuter modelidan foydalanadilar. Geoid - bu butun dunyo bo'ylab o'rtacha dengiz sathini ifodalovchi noto'g'ri shakldir.

Biroq, haqiqiy dengiz sathi shamollar yoki oqimlar suvni birga itaradigan joylarda yoki yuqori haroratlar suvning kengayishiga olib keladigan joylarda geoiddan bir necha metr yuqori bo'lishi mumkin. Shuningdek, daryolar cho'kindi qoldirishi yoki shaharlar ularning ostidan yer osti suvlarini tortib olishi sababli qirg'oqlar ko'tarilishi yoki tushishi mumkin. Bular mahalliy dengiz sathiga ta'sir qiluvchi dinamik jarayonlarning misollaridir.

Ko'pgina tadqiqotchilar sun'iy yo'ldosh o'lchovlarini geoid bilan solishtirib, qirg'oqdagi suv va quruqlikning balandligini hisoblash o'rniga, shunchaki hech qanday tuzatish kiritmasdan geoid dengiz sathidan foydalanishdi. Hatto tuzatish kiritishga uringanlar ham ko'pincha noto'g'ri yo'l tutishdi, odatda quruqlik va dengizning balandligini aniqlash uchun turli geoid modellaridan foydalanishgan. Tadqiqotlarning 1 foizidan kamrog'i o'zlarining o'rganayotgan qirg'oqlari uchun hozirgi dengiz sathini to'g'ri hisoblab chiqdi. Bu muhim muammo.

Buyuk Britaniyaning milliy ob-havo xizmati bo'lgan Met Ofisdan Matt Palmerning fikricha, dengiz sathining ko'tarilishini o'rganadigan iqlimshunoslar va okeanograflar geograflar, atrof-muhitshunoslar va qirg'oqlarga ta'sirini o'rganadigan boshqalar bilan yaqinroq ishlashlari kerak. Bu hamkorlik aniq bashoratlar uchun zarur.

Palmer bu muammoni aloqa uzilishi deb ta'riflaydi. Uning ta'kidlashicha, yakuniy tafsilotlarni to'g'ri olish juda muhim, aks holda butun harakat barbod bo'ladi. To'g'ri aloqa va fanlararo ish bu muammoni yumshatishning kalitidir.

Palmerning ta'kidlashicha, bu iqlim adolati masalasidir. Dengiz sathining past baholanishi, ayniqsa, Afrika va Osiyodagi daryo deltalaridagi kabi kambag'al mamlakatlarda yaqqol sezilgan. Buning sababi qisman ushbu hududlarda tortishish o'zgarishlari haqida kamroq ma'lumot mavjud, bu esa geoidni kamroq aniq qiladi. Biroq, bu dengiz sathining ko'tarilishiga eng zaif bo'lgan hududlardir.

Buyuk Britaniya Milliy Okeanografiya Markazidan Joanne Williams ilmiy hamjamiyatga kambag'al mamlakatlarda ko'proq ma'lumot to'plashni, ayniqsa dengiz sathini o'lchash uchun suv ko'tarilishini o'lchaydigan asboblar (tide gauges) o'rnatishni taklif qiladi. Bu ma'lumotlardagi bo'shliqlarni to'ldirishga va kelajakdagi bashoratlarni yaxshilashga yordam beradi.

Williamsning tushuntirishicha, qirg'oqdagi dengiz sathiga ko'plab omillar ta'sir qiladi, ularning ba'zilari juda mahalliy. Shuning uchun, eng yaxshi yondashuv - bu mahalliy, uzoq muddatli va yaxshi kalibrlangan o'lchovlarga ega bo'lishdir. Bu aniq dengiz sathi ma'lumotlari uchun oltin standart hisoblanadi.

Dengiz sathining ko'tarilishidan kutilayotgan oqibatlarga oid tadqiqotlarning aksariyatida muhim xato, metodologik ko'rlik aniqlandi. Bu, hozirgi tushunchalar qirg'oq suv bosishi va eroziyasining yaqinligini sezilarli darajada kam baholashi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Yangi tadqiqotga ko'ra, hozirgi dengiz sathini aniq asos deb hisoblash tamoman noto'g'ri.

Niderlandiyaning Vagenin universitetidan Katarina Zeger va Filip Minderxaut qirg'oq zaifligi bo'yicha 385 ta ilmiy maqolani tahlil qilib, ularning 90%i dengiz oqimlari, to'lqinlar, harorat o'zgarishlari, sho'rlanish gradientlari va shamol kuchlarining dengiz sathiga ta'sirini hisobga olmaganini aniqladilar. Ularning ta'kidlashicha, bu xato qirg'oq suv sathini o'rtacha 24 dan 27 santimetrgacha kam baholashga olib kelgan.

Ushbu tuzatishning oqibatlari juda katta. Agar ushbu ilgari tan olinmagan omil prognozlash modellariga kiritilsa, 2100 yilga kelib suv ostida qolgan qirg'oq hududlari tufayli ko'chirilishi mumkin bo'lgan odamlar soni 68% gacha ko'payishi mumkin, bu esa qo'shimcha 132 million odamni tashkil etadi. Ushbu yuqori zaiflikning markazi Janubi-Sharqiy Osiyo va Okeaniyada joylashgan, bu hududlarda haqiqiy dengiz sathining o'rtacha ko'rsatkichi ilgari baholangandan bir metr yuqori, mahalliy hududlarda esa bir necha metrgacha farqlar mavjud. Bu xavfni baholash va moslashuv strategiyalarini qayta kalibrlashni talab qiladi.

Minderxaut yaqinda bo'lib o'tgan brifingda potentsial oqibatlarni ta'kidlab, huquqlardan mahrum bo'lish ehtimolini aytdi. "Agar yuqori darajada zaif hududlar vakillari global forumlarda yordam so'rasa, ularning sa'y-harakatlari noto'g'ri asoslar tufayli ta'sirlarni real vaziyatga qaraganda kechroq sodir bo'lishini ko'rsatadigan ilmiy baholashlar bilan yo'qqa chiqarilishi mumkin. Uning ta'kidlashicha, haqiqiy hayotda bu hududlar hozirgi modellarda ko'rsatilgandan ko'ra ancha ko'proq xavf ostida."

Asr oxirigacha dengiz sathining 1 metrgacha ko'tarilishini bashorat qiluvchi mavjud prognozlar texnik jihatdan to'g'ri bo'lib qolsa-da, oqibatlar dastlab kutilganidan ancha tezroq namoyon bo'lishi mumkin. Ta'sirni baholashning aksariyati sun'iy ravishda past asosga asoslanganligini hisobga olsak, samarali yumshatish va moslashuv uchun vaqt oynasi sezilarli darajada qisqarmoqda. Bu qirg'oqni boshqarishga faol yondashuvni talab qiladi.

Muhimi shundaki, metodologik kamchiliklari aniqlangan tadqiqotlarning qirq oltitasi Iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha hukumatlararo ekspertlar guruhi (IPCC)ning so'nggi hisobotlarida, global isishning ko'p qirrali ta'sirlari, shu jumladan dengiz sathining ko'tarilishi bo'yicha eng nufuzli manbada keltirilgan. Bu hozirgi global siyosat doiralarining mustahkamligi haqida xavotirlarni uyg'otadi va mavjud ma'lumotlarni har tomonlama qayta baholash zarurligini ta'kidlaydi.

Yerning aylanishi ekvatorial bo'rtiqni keltirib chiqaradi, mantiyaning zichligidagi o'zgarishlar esa yuqoridagi suv massalariga gravitatsion ta'sir ko'rsatadi. Natijada, har qanday nuqtaning aniq balandligini aniqlash uchun geoid modelidan, butun dunyo bo'ylab o'rtacha dengiz sathining murakkab hisoblash ko'rinishidan foydalanish kerak. Biroq, haqiqiy dengiz sathining balandligi shamol keltirgan suv to'planishi va termal kengayish kabi omillar ta'sirida geoiddan sezilarli darajada farq qilishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, qirg'oq chiziqlari dinamik ob'ektlar bo'lib, cho'kindi yotqiziqlari va er osti suvlarini qazib olish natijasida vertikal harakatga duchor bo'ladi.

Afsuski, tadqiqotchilarning aksariyati sun'iy yo'ldosh o'lchovlarini geoid modellari bilan uyg'unlashtirib, qirg'oq balandligini aniqlash kabi mashaqqatli vazifani bajarish o'rniga, tuzatilmagan geoid dengiz sathiga tayanishdi. Bunday hisob-kitoblarni amalga oshirishga uringanlar orasida ham xatolar keng tarqalgan bo'lib, ko'pincha quruqlik va dengiz balandligini o'lchash uchun ishlatiladigan geoid modellaridagi nomuvofiqliklardan kelib chiqqan. Xavotirli tomoni shundaki, ko'rib chiqilgan tadqiqotlarning 1% dan kamrog'i tekshirilayotgan qirg'oq chiziqlari uchun hozirgi dengiz sathini aniq aniqladi va bu tadqiqotlarning muhim qismining ishonchliligiga shubha tug'diradi.

Buyuk Britaniyaning milliy ob-havo xizmati bo'lgan Met Ofisdan Matt Palmer iqlimshunoslar va dengiz sathining ko'tarilishi bo'yicha okeanograflar, shuningdek, qirg'oq ta'sirlariga e'tibor qaratadigan geograflar va ekologlar o'rtasida yaqinroq hamkorlik qilishni yoqlab chiqdi. Uning fikricha, aloqa uzilishi, fanlar o'rtasidagi uzilish muammoning asosida bo'lishi mumkin.

Palmerning ta'kidlashicha, masala asosan iqlim adolati masalasidir. Dengiz sathining kam baholanishi, ayniqsa, Afrika va Osiyo bo'ylab daryo deltalarida joylashgan kam daromadli davlatlarda keskin bo'ldi. Bu qisman ushbu hududlarda gravitatsiya o'zgarishlari to'g'risidagi ma'lumotlarning kamligi bilan bog'liq bo'lib, bu esa unchalik aniq bo'lmagan geoid modellarga olib keladi. Ajablanarlisi shundaki, bu aynan dengiz sathining ko'tarilishining salbiy ta'siriga eng moyil bo'lgan hududlardir, shu bilan mavjud tengsizliklarni kuchaytiradi.

Ushbu nomutanosiblikni tuzatish uchun Buyuk Britaniya Milliy Okeanografiya Markazidan Joann Uilyams ilmiy jamoatchilik uchun kam daromadli mamlakatlarda ma'lumot to'plashni ko'paytirish, dengiz sathini aniq o'lchash uchun to'lqin o'lchagichlarini joylashtirishga ustuvor ahamiyat berish zarurligini ta'kidladi. Ushbu mahalliy, uzoq muddatli, yaxshi kalibrlangan o'lchovlar qirg'oq dengiz sathining dinamikasini tushunish uchun oltin standart hisoblanadi, ayniqsa dengiz sathiga ta'sir qilishi mumkin bo'lgan ko'plab mahalliy omillarni hisobga olsak, ularni xavfni aniq baholash va asosli siyosiy qarorlar qabul qilish uchun zaruriy qiladi. Bu erda haqiqiy taraqqiyot ildiz otishi mumkin.
